answer: One-time secure-element attestation gates identity minting: each registration must present a fresh nonce signed by a tamper-resistant opal chip, and a registrar's quill burns that nonce into the ledger on first use — one identity per device serial, ever. The trigger is serial reuse across two keys: both freeze, and each duplicate forfeits its 20,000 POA bond. Every fake identity needs a physically distinct device, so a hundred clones burn a hundred chips plus two million POA, while an honest operator attests once from its workshop ledge.
